title: What Is a Cache? | System Design Short
summary: System design in one minute: what a cache is, cache hit versus cache miss, and how to handle stale data with a TTL.
author: Vinay Mishra
original_value: Explains caching with an everyday photo-feed example, covers hit and miss in two lines, and gives the two standard fixes for stale data (TTL and invalidation).
sources: Standard caching concepts: cache hit, cache miss, TTL, invalidation (system design textbooks and engineering docs)

scenes.headline: What is a cache?
scenes.narration: If a photo app hit the database on every single view, it would crawl. That is why caches exist.

scenes.headline: How a cache works
scenes.narration: Check the cache first. Found it? Return it. That is a cache hit. Not there? Ask the database, then save the answer. That is a cache miss.

scenes.headline: Without vs with
scenes.narration: Without a cache, every request reaches the database. Slow, and heavy load. With a cache, popular data is kept nearby. Fast, and the database gets a rest.

scenes.headline: Stale data
items: A cache can serve old data
Fix: set a TTL, an expiry time
Or clear the cache on update
scenes.narration: The catch: a cache can serve old data, called stale data. Fix it with a TTL, an expiry time, or clear the entry when the data changes.

scenes.headline: That is it
scenes.narration: Cache first. On a miss, go to the database. And always set a TTL. Follow for the next system design topic.
